topics.title: 1. Creational Patterns
topics.description: Object creation mechanisms that increase flexibility and reuse of existing code: Singleton, Factory Method, Builder, Prototype, and Abstract Factory.

subtopics.title: Singleton Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Ensures a class has only one instance while providing a global access point to this instance.

subtopics.title: Factory Method Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

subtopics.title: Builder Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create various representations.

subtopics.title: Prototype Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Specifies the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance, creating new objects by copying this prototype.

subtopics.title: Abstract Factory Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.

topics.title: 2. Structural Patterns
topics.description: Assembling objects and classes into larger, flexible structures while keeping systems efficient and decoupled: Adapter, Facade, Decorator, Proxy, Composite, Bridge, and Flyweight.

subtopics.title: Adapter Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Allows objects with incompatible interfaces to collaborate by converting the interface of a class into another interface clients expect.

subtopics.title: Facade Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Provides a unified, simplified interface to a complex subsystem, making the subsystem easier to use.

subtopics.title: Decorator Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically, providing a flexible alternative to subclassing for extending functionality.

subtopics.title: Proxy Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Provides a placeholder or surrogate for another object to control access to it.

subtopics.title: Composite Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies, letting clients treat individual objects and compositions uniformly.

subtopics.title: Bridge Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independently.

subtopics.title: Flyweight Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Minimizes memory usage by sharing as much data as possible with similar objects.

topics.title: 3. Behavioral Patterns
topics.description: Algorithms, communication, and assignment of responsibilities between objects: Strategy, Observer, Command, Template Method, Iterator, State, Chain of Responsibility, Mediator, Memento, Visitor, and Interpreter.

subtopics.title: Strategy Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable at runtime.

subtopics.title: Observer Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Defines a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified automatically.

subtopics.title: Command Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Encapsulates a request as an object, thereby letting you parameterize clients with different requests, queue or log requests, and support undoable operations.

subtopics.title: Template Method Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in an operation, deferring some steps to subclasses without changing the algorithm's structure.

subtopics.title: Iterator Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Provides a way to access the elements of an aggregate object sequentially without exposing its underlying representation.

subtopics.title: State Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes. The object will appear to change its class.

subtopics.title: Chain of Responsibility Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Passes requests along a chain of handlers; upon receiving a request, each handler decides either to process it or pass it to the next handler.

subtopics.title: Mediator Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact, preventing them from referring to each other explicitly.

subtopics.title: Memento Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Without violating encapsulation, captures and externalizes an object's internal state so that the object can be restored to this state later.

subtopics.title: Visitor Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure, letting you define a new operation without changing the classes of the elements.

subtopics.title: Interpreter Pattern
subtopics.subtitle: Given a language, defines a representation for its grammar along with an interpreter that uses the representation to interpret sentences in the language.
